 Is Bayern Munich considering a sale of Jamal Musiala?
 ﻿Karl-Heinz Rummenigge weighs Bayern’s financial reality as Jamal Musiala navigates injury setbacks.
 by CSmith1919 Updated Nov 21, 2026, 5:45 AM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images) Getty Images Part Of Bayern Munich vs. FC Köln: 2026/27 Bundesliga full coverage see all updates CSmith1919 Chuck Smith is the site manager for Bavarian Football Works, where he began writing in 2017. He is the author of The Daily Schmankerl, the longest-running daily Bayern Munich column in English, and also writes The Weekend Warm-Up. In addition to covering Bayern Munich news and providing commentary on Bayern Munich, the Bundesliga, and the German national team. He brings more than 30 years of sports-writing experience to the site. Over the course of his career, he has written for numerous newspapers and websites. Could Jamal Musiala’s future at Bayern Munich eventually become a financial question rather than simply a footballing one? Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has offered a sobering perspective on the situation, acknowledging that the club may eventually have to consider difficult decisions if the midfielder cannot return to his previous level following his injury problems.
 Rummenigge does not appear to believe a transfer is a realistic solution under the current circumstances, either for Bayern or a potential buying club.
 ”I can’t imagine Jamal leaving the club, or any other club being willing to sign him under these circumstances. That’s a problem. I think we’ve handled the situation with the player very sensitively, and we’re all interested in seeing him return, ideally in the best possible condition. But what happens if that doesn’t happen? Then, of course, we still have to consider the financial implications. And I think that’s a decision the executive board and supervisory board may unfortunately have to make,” said Rummenigge (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ).
 Those comments introduce another uncomfortable dimension to Bayern’s Musiala dilemma. The club has invested heavily in securing his future, but his recurring injury problems have complicated the equation.
 For now, Bayern clearly wants Musiala back and performing at his best. However, Rummenigge is acknowledging that sentiment cannot completely override financial reality, and the club’s leadership may eventually have some difficult decisions to make.
